body: [{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-74e2-93c6-4957d4556128","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-74e2-93c6-4957d4556128\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**A stacked pull-request edge exists as an explicit opt-in dependency: a task declared stacked on its blocker dispatches at the blocker\\u0027s Delivered rather than its merge, builds on the blocker\\u0027s branch, opens its pull request against that branch, and is mechanically retargeted and replayed onto the base branch when the parent merges** (renumbered from a duplicate #140 to #142 and then to #143 across 2026-09-07\\u0027s rebase onto main, when main was found to have independently claimed #140 for the per-project dispatch ceiling above, #141 for the cross-project rotation beside it, and #142 for the tracker claim gate directly above; Brian\\u0027s direction 2026-08-28, promoting idea 634e49bb; cohesion ruling the same day; slice one of two). Why: for stacked work the platform did not participate at all \\u2014 the field evidence is two real stacks in one day (2026-08-31, ARX-5510 with eight pull requests and ARX-4836 with two), both driven entirely by hand, which is a participation failure rather than friction. The edge is \\u0060TaskAdded.StackedOnTaskId\\u0060 / \\u0060TaskRevised.StackedOnTaskId\\u0060 (\\u0060h9k task add --stacked-on\\u0060, \\u0060h9k task revise --stacked-on\\u0060 / \\u0060--clear-stacked-on\\u0060), and **the tool never infers it from an ordinary \\u0060--blocked-by\\u0060** \\u2014 Brian\\u0027s cohesion ruling: a stacked edge is reserved for tasks cohesive in feature set, slices of one idea (the interactive-mode pair 34a618a6/d917e161 is the canonical example), and the declaration is always a human\\u0027s. It is an invariant, enforced rather than repaired by \\u0060TaskDecider.VetStackedEdge\\u0060, that the stacked parent is **also** a member of \\u0060BlockedBy\\u0060: that is what lets the publish-time cycle walk and the unmet-dependency bookkeeping see the edge without either knowing stacking exists, and the CLI merges the option into the blocked-by set so a human types the parent once. Six behaviours follow, and a plain blocked-by task gets none of them. **(1) Dispatchable at Delivered.** \\u0060StackedEdgeRules\\u0060 is the one home for \\u0022does this blocker hold this dependent back\\u0022, asked by both \\u0060TaskDecider.Assign\\u0060 (which freezes the unmet set) and \\u0060TaskDependencyResolver\\u0060 (which re-evaluates it every sweep) so the two can never disagree; for the declared parent it reads \\u0060TaskDependency.BlocksStackedChild\\u0060 (Done with a pull request open) instead of true closeout, and \\u0060IsDeadForStackedChild\\u0060 instead of \\u0060IsDead\\u0060 \\u2014 a Done parent whose merge observation will never arrive has still delivered the branch and pull request its child is built on, so a dead-blocker hold there would park the child for a hold that never applied to it, while a Done parent that never delivered one at all (its pull request closed unmerged, or no pull request ever) is dead for either kind of edge. **(2) Cut from the parent\\u0027s branch head.** \\u0060StackedBaseResolver\\u0060 resolves the base once at dispatch, from the parent\\u0027s own current run (the branch name lives on the run, never the task), and \\u0060RunLauncher\\u0060 freezes it on \\u0060RunDispatched.BaseBranch\\u0060 \\u2014 blank meaning \\u0022the project\\u0027s own base branch\\u0022, which is every ordinary run and every stream written before the field, so nothing needs a backfill and nothing about the unstacked case changes. Every shape the resolver cannot honour (a parent already closed out, one with no run carrying a branch) falls back to the project\\u0027s base with the reason logged, because a stacked child that lands on main is an ordinary pull request a human can still merge while one refused outright is work that never runs. **(3) The pull request opens against that branch** (\\u0060PullRequestOpener\\u0060 reads \\u0060RunDetails.BaseBranchOr\\u0060), forming the GitHub stack. **(4) The diff is the child\\u0027s own delta.** The recorded base is what \\u0060ReviewEngine\\u0060, \\u0060AgentPromptBuilder\\u0060 and \\u0060WorkPromptBuilder\\u0060 all read instead of \\u0060project.BaseBranch\\u0060 \\u2014 the review packet\\u0027s range, the pre-final-pass rebase\\u0027s target, the build session\\u0027s own self-review hunt, and the end-of-work recompose\\u0027s fork point. The recompose is the load-bearing one and the reason this is not cosmetic: a stacked child whose recompose reset to \\u0060merge-base origin/main HEAD\\u0060 would rewrite the parent\\u0027s commits as if they were its own history. **(5) Not at the merge bar while un-retargeted.** \\u0060RunDetails.StackedOnBranch\\u0060/\\u0060AwaitsStackedRetarget\\u0060 is the mechanical reading, and it works from the blank-means-the-project\\u0027s-own invariant alone, which is what lets the CLI\\u0027s attention and phase composers answer it with no \\u0060ProjectDetails\\u0060 in hand; \\u0060CloseoutEngine.TryAutoMergeAsync\\u0060 refuses a pre-approved child on it as a visible wait rather than a park (design ruling 3\\u0027s own terms, #135), and the board never says \\u0022the merge is yours\\u0022 about a pull request whose merge would land its commits on its parent\\u0027s branch. **(6) Retarget and mechanical replay.** Checked from the child\\u0027s own sweep, ahead of the conflict read (GitHub will often report the child CONFLICTING as a *consequence* of the parent moving, and #131\\u0027s mechanical rebase already refuses a pull request whose base is not the project\\u0027s own, so without this the correct operation would never be reached and the child would take a full review lap for a conflict that is not its own). \\u0060StackedParentWatch\\u0060 observes the parent from git \\u2014 \\u0060origin/\\u003Cparent\\u003E\\u0060 first, falling back to \\u0060refs/pull/\\u003Cn\\u003E/head\\u0060, which GitHub keeps after the branch is deleted and is the only reason a child whose parent\\u0027s closeout already ran is still observable \\u2014 and answers Aligned, ParentMerged, ParentMoved, ParentMergedElsewhere, or Unobservable, never treating a failed read as agreement. The boundary the replay drops the parent\\u0027s commits at is the child run\\u0027s own **recorded** fork point (\\u0060RunDispatched.BaseCommit\\u0060, observed at the cut by \\u0060GitWorktreeManager.CreateAsync\\u0060, carried forward unchanged by any follow-up that resumes the branch, and replaced by the commit each replay is dispatched to land on) \\u2014 deliberately not \\u0060git merge-base\\u0060, which was how this was first written and is wrong in exactly the case the force-push arm exists for. A force-push rewrites the history the child shares with its parent, so the merge base of the child and the parent\\u0027s NEW head collapses back to the base branch, and a replay from there re-applies the child\\u0027s copy of the parent\\u0027s OLD commit against its new one, conflicting on the parent\\u0027s own content. That was found by running the replay against a scratch repository during this task\\u0027s own self-review rather than by reading it, which is the whole argument for that phase\\u0027s execute-don\\u0027t-proofread hunt. A child whose run recorded no fork point (a stream written before the field) reads Unobservable and is left alone rather than replayed on a guess. Both arguments of the replay\\u0027s \\u0060git rebase --onto \\u003Conto\\u003E \\u003Cupstream\\u003E\\u0060 are exact commits for the same reason: \\u0060TaskReopened.StackReplayOntoCommit\\u0060 is the freshly observed head the replay lands on, so a run that waits to be claimed still lands where closeout actually looked rather than wherever the ref drifted to \\u2014 a base branch that moves in between is the ordinary freshness machinery\\u0027s business, as it is for every run. ParentMerged retargets through \\u0060IPullRequestInspector.RetargetAsync\\u0060 (the provider seam every other write here uses, idempotent, so a retry after a lost fence race is safe) and only then dispatches; a failed retarget dispatches nothing and records why, because replaying onto the base while the pull request is still aimed at a deleted branch would leave a pull request nobody can merge and no dispatch coming to fix it. ParentMoved \\u2014 the parent\\u0027s branch moved to a head the child does not contain while the child was Delivered, ordinarily a review lap folding fixes into its own commits and force-pushing \\u2014 dispatches the identical replay onto the new head with the base untouched: same operation, different \\u0060--onto\\u0060, which is why both share one \\u0060FollowUpKind.StackReplay\\u0060 and one budget. The replay is **mechanical by construction, not by promise**: \\u0060RunLauncher\\u0060 forces \\u0060ReviewStageComposition.None\\u0060 for that kind, which is exactly \\u0022the gates still run, no reviewer ever reads the diff\\u0022 (#129) \\u2014 git replaying commits that already passed review is not new intent \\u2014 and its prompt (\\u0060AgentPromptBuilder.BuildStackReplay\\u0060) names the boundary literally and forbids improving anything noticed in passing, since nothing downstream will catch it. Bounded by the child\\u0027s **own** rebase budget (\\u0060TaskAggregate.StackReplaysDispatched\\u0060, \\u0060DaemonOptions.MaxStackReplayRuns\\u0060, default 12), deliberately **not** folded into the lifetime closeout ceiling: a replay answers the parent moving, which this task neither caused nor can prevent, so charging it to the child\\u0027s review budget would let a parent that force-pushes half a dozen times spend the child\\u0027s whole budget before one of its own review laps ever ran. Past the cap the child parks with the base untouched, leaving a coherent stack a human can finish by hand. **Four corrections from this diff\\u0027s own independent pre-PR review (cycle 1), all one root \\u2014 the in-run machinery pointed at the parent as a *ref* while the closeout machinery carefully recorded *commits*.** First, the end-of-work recompose and the self-review hunt name the recorded fork point as a **literal commit** rather than computing \\u0060merge-base origin/\\u003Cparent\\u003E HEAD\\u0060: the merge base against a parent force-pushed mid-session collapses *below* the child\\u0027s real fork point, so the mixed reset would dissolve the parent\\u0027s commits along with the child\\u0027s and the tree-identity check could never catch it (a mixed reset never moves the tree) \\u2014 the same wrongness the boundary already avoided, one layer up. Second, the pre-final-pass rebase gate is **skipped outright** for a stacked child instead of retargeted at the parent branch: a plain \\u0060git rebase origin/\\u003Cparent\\u003E\\u0060 is the exact operation the boundary design proves wrong, and closeout\\u0027s own mechanical replay is what answers a parent that moved. Third, the boundary is observed directly where git can still answer it \\u2014 a merged parent whose head the child\\u0027s branch still contains **is** the boundary, read fresh \\u2014 and falls back to the record only for the force-pushed case, because a record made at dispatch can be moved out from under by a rebase; \\u0060RunRebasedOntoBase\\u0060\\u0027s apply now advances \\u0060BaseCommit\\u0060 for the same reason. Fourth, every park verdict the replay dispatch is subject to is asked *before* the retarget\\u0027s \\u0060gh pr edit --base\\u0060, not after, so no park can leave a pull request moved onto the base with the replay undone. **A fifth, from cycle 2, the same root one layer further out**: the *closeout-dispatched* follow-up prompts still pointed at the parent as a ref. A child whose parent could not be observed that sweep (\\u0060Unobservable\\u0060) but which GitHub reports CONFLICTING falls through to a \\u0060FollowUpKind.Rebase\\u0060 judgment session, and that prompt told it to run the very \\u0060git rebase origin/\\u003Cparent\\u003E\\u0060 the pre-final-pass gate refuses \\u2014 it now teaches the replay instead, \\u0060git rebase --onto origin/\\u003Cparent\\u003E \\u003Crecorded fork point\\u003E\\u0060, and disputes rather than guesses when no fork point was ever recorded; the same holds for every narrative fixup-and-autosquash instruction a stacked child\\u0027s follow-up carries (review-feedback, failing-checks, the replay\\u0027s own gate fix), each of which now names an observed commit \\u2014 the recorded fork point where nothing moves the branch, the commit a replay landed on where something did \\u2014 because a fold against a force-pushed parent rewrites its already-reviewed commits as the child\\u0027s own authored history and the tree-identity check cannot always catch it. \\u0060BuildPreFinalPassRebase\\u0060 keeps the plain wording deliberately: the gate above it refuses a stacked base before any git call, so no stacked run reaches that prompt at all. The CLI\\u0027s own two interactive claims record \\u0060BaseCommit\\u0060 and thread the base through their prompts exactly as \\u0060RunLauncher\\u0060 does \\u2014 without it, a CLI-claimed child was permanently \\u0060Unobservable\\u0060 and its \\u0060h9k task start\\u0060 prompt recomposed against \\u0060origin/main\\u0060. **A sixth root, from cycle 4, and the last surface holding the ref: the *review* prompts.** The lens, verify-cycle and fix-session prompts still named \\u0060origin/\\u003Cparent\\u003E\\u0060 as the range they read and \\u2014 the part that makes it more than a stale read \\u2014 as the range that decides \\u0060in-scope\\u0060 from \\u0060out-of-scope\\u0060, so a parent force-pushed during the child\\u0027s review window collapsed that three-dot merge base to the project base, had the reviewer grade parent-owned defects as this pull request\\u0027s own, and had the fix session edit the parent\\u0027s code on the child\\u0027s branch. All three now carry the recorded fork point (\\u0060ReviewMechanicsOverride.ForkPointCommit\\u0060, \\u0060RunDetails.StackedForkPoint\\u0060), falling back to the parent branch only where nothing was ever recorded, and a fourth source-level guard scan (\\u0060StackedBaseBranchGuardTests\\u0060) refuses a review prompt handed the branch without the commit. Three more of the same root landed with it. A run that RESUMES this task\\u0027s existing branch \\u2014 a follow-up, or a retry that resumed \\u0060RetryBranch\\u0060 \\u2014 now inherits BOTH base facts from the run before it (\\u0060StackedBaseResolver.ResumedBaseAsync\\u0060) rather than re-resolving the branch: a resumed checkout reports no start point at all, so a retry recorded a blank fork point over one the failed run had observed, and re-resolving the base asked the resolver about the PARENT\\u0027s current state, which answers \\u0022the project\\u0027s base\\u0022 for a branch still physically carrying the parent\\u0027s commits and would have disarmed the retarget, the replay and the merge bar for good. \\u0060StackedParentWatch\\u0060 now confirms the branch actually contains the recorded fork point before replaying from it, because for a replay run that field is a dispatch-time prediction (the commit the replay was TOLD to land on) and a replay that took its prompt\\u0027s sanctioned abort leaves it naming a commit the branch never reached \\u2014 Unobservable is the honest answer there. And every \\u0022commits beyond the base\\u0022 count (\\u0060VerificationRunner\\u0060\\u0027s no-commit check, \\u0060h9k task deliver\\u0060/\\u0060release\\u0060/\\u0060delegate\\u0060) now takes the SMALLEST count any candidate boundary reports rather than the first that resolves: a two-dot count is inflated by every commit its boundary does not reach and never deflated, both candidates go stale in that one direction and neither always, so the smallest is both the most accurate answer and the safe direction for a check whose job is catching a session that committed nothing. **Three more from cycle 6, and the first of them is the feature\\u0027s own mainline race rather than an edge case.** A stacked child dispatches at its parent\\u0027s *Delivered*, so the parent\\u0027s merge \\u2014 a human\\u0027s or the daemon\\u0027s pre-approved auto-merge \\u2014 routinely lands during the child\\u0027s hours-long build and review pipeline, and the parent\\u0027s closeout deletes its branch everywhere unconditionally: \\u0060gh pr create --base \\u003Cthat branch\\u003E\\u0060 was then a raw 422 that failed the run and the task with a message naming none of this, and the retry inherited the same frozen base (correctly \\u2014 a resumed branch\\u0027s base is a fact about the branch) and failed identically, forever, because every retarget and replay mechanism here is reachable only from closeout\\u0027s inspection of an *already-open* pull request. \\u0060PullRequestOpener\\u0060 now asks origin whether that branch is still there before aiming a pull request at it, and opens against the project\\u0027s base when it is not \\u2014 exactly where the retarget would have put it \\u2014 while deliberately leaving the run\\u0027s recorded base saying the parent\\u0027s branch, because the branch still physically carries the parent\\u0027s commits and the replay that drops them is still owed; the next sweep observes the merged parent, records the retarget over a pull request already on the right base (\\u0060gh pr edit --base\\u0060 is idempotent), and dispatches the replay. Only git\\u0027s documented \\u0022no matching ref\\u0022 moves the base: an origin that could not be *read* is not a branch that is gone, and guessing one away would aim a stacked pull request at the wrong base while the parent is still open. Second, the containment check cycle 4 gave \\u0060StackedParentWatch\\u0060 now also runs where else that record is re-asserted \\u2014 a run that resumes the branch carries the recorded fork point forward only while the branch still contains it, and records none at all when it does not, so a replay that took its prompt\\u0027s sanctioned abort can no longer hand the next rebase session \\u0060git rebase --onto origin/\\u003Cparent\\u003E \\u003Ca commit the branch never landed on\\u003E\\u0060 or scope a review lap\\u0027s diff from there; the stacked rebase prompt\\u0027s own verification became containment rather than mere existence with it, and disputes when it fails, which is the honest answer an unobserved boundary already had. Third, \\u0060BuildStackReplay\\u0060 hard-coded the narrative commit style into its gate-fix instruction while \\u0060RunLauncher\\u0060 held the project\\u0027s resolved style at the call site: on an append-style project a replay \\u2014 the one follow-up nothing reviews \\u2014 was told to fold a gate fix into its owning commit, rewriting history against the convention that project declared, and told something false about the project while doing it. **Two more from cycle 8, both against cycle 6\\u0027s own corrections.** The \\u0022parent branch gone\\u0022 warning that accompanies the pull-request-open fallback named five placeholders and passed three arguments: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging binds placeholders *positionally per occurrence* and never deduplicates a repeated name, so \\u0060LogWarning\\u0060 itself threw a \\u0060FormatException\\u0060 \\u2014 aborting the fallback before it returned the base it had just picked, failing the run on \\u0022An error occurred while writing to logger(s)\\u0022, and reinstating verbatim the fails-forever retry loop that fallback exists to end, in exactly the mainline race it was written for. Nothing caught it because the new tests exercise only the pure \\u0060OpenBaseFor\\u0060 decision and every other test path logs through \\u0060NullLogger\\u0060, which never formats; the warning now lives in a named method a test renders through a logger that actually calls the formatter. Second, the resumed fork point\\u0027s containment check landed on \\u0060RunLauncher\\u0060 alone, while \\u0060StackedBaseResolver.ResumedBaseAsync\\u0060\\u0027s own doc \\u2014 and this entry\\u0027s cycle-6 text above \\u2014 claim it runs wherever the record is re-asserted: the CLI\\u0027s two interactive claims still asserted it unconditionally, so a human claiming a failed replay\\u0027s task with \\u0060h9k task start\\u0060 or \\u0060h9k task work\\u0060 got a recompose boundary and self-review ranges computed from a commit the branch never reached. All three doors now share one implementation (\\u0060TaskWorkCommand.ResumedForkPointAsync\\u0060, beside the \\u0060CheckoutFreshOrRetryAsync\\u0060 those two doors already share), which is the standing shape for this: three doors reading a resumed branch, one answer. **Five more from the independent pre-PR review of 2026-09-07 (the cycle after cycle 8, whose own numbering restarted at 1), and four of them are the never-guess rule applied to what this feature *records* rather than to what it does.** First and the only one above the fix bar: \\u0060IsDelivered\\u0060 read Done-plus-a-pull-request-URL, and a pull request the monitor observed CLOSED without merging leaves exactly that shape forever \\u2014 \\u0060RecordClosedAsync\\u0060 writes the closure onto the RUN\\u0027s stream and leaves the task Done carrying the URL it always had. A parent a human closed unmerged therefore read Delivered, released a stacked child that had not dispatched yet, and sent it through its whole build-and-review pipeline onto a branch whose pull request can never merge, to sit off the merge bar promising a retarget nothing could ever perform; \\u0060IsDeadForStackedChild\\u0060\\u0027s Failed-or-Abandoned enumeration did not catch it either, because that rule\\u0027s own rationale assumed the child had already dispatched, which the not-yet-released case disproves. Both now read the run\\u0027s recorded failure reason, and the third arm is the general one: a Done parent that \\u0060BlocksStackedChild\\u0060 still holds back has left its own lifecycle without passing either bar and is dead, which also covers \\u0060h9k task resolve\\u0060\\u0027s attestation exit (#27) landing Done with no pull request at all. Second, \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 and \\u0060h9k task assign\\u0060 marked a stacked parent met at Delivered \\u0022closed out\\u0022 \\u2014 a closeout nothing observed, printed two lines under the sentence saying this edge is met at Delivered and beside the row\\u0027s own Delivered word, which is the 2026-08-22 word-versus-mark incident one bar further down; the met arm gained its own wording, and the closeout word is kept for an observed closeout. Third, ParentMoved\\u0027s own account asserted the parent \\u0022was force-pushed\\u0022, but \\u0060--is-ancestor\\u0060\\u0027s exit 1 is returned identically by a commit merely appended since the child was cut (an append-style project\\u0027s checks-fix lap) and nothing here reads a reflog that could tell them apart \\u2014 that detail becomes the reopen\\u0027s recorded reason and any later park\\u0027s obstruction summary, so it now reports the move and names both shapes. Fourth, the pull-request-open fallback\\u0027s warning asserted the parent\\u0027s \\u0022pull request merged while this branch was still building\\u0022 from \\u0060ls-remote\\u0060\\u0027s missing-ref code alone, which a parent branch that was never pushed returns just as readily \\u2014 the shape a child claimed ahead of its parent with \\u0060--acknowledge-unmet-dependencies\\u0060 produces, an explicitly supported override \\u2014 so it now reports the absence and names both shapes; the behaviour was right for either. Fifth, the ParentMerged arm retargeted onto \\u0060project.BaseBranch\\u0060 unconditionally, which is false for a mid-stack parent merged by hand while still aimed at ITS parent\\u0027s branch: the child\\u0027s correct base is one level up, GitHub\\u0027s own retarget already put it there, and overriding that would have replayed the child mechanically onto a base missing the grandparent\\u0027s work in a session no reviewer reads. The watch now reads where the parent\\u0027s work actually landed off the parent\\u0027s own run and answers \\u0060ParentMergedElsewhere\\u0060, which parks the child with its stack intact before any git call or retarget \\u2014 the honest answer, since ordering across three or more levels is out of this slice by design and this platform\\u0027s own merge bar never merges an un-retargeted pull request, so nothing automatic produced that state. **One more, from the independent pre-PR review of task d28763ca (2026-09-15), against the fifth correction\\u0027s own text just above.** That correction read the parent\\u0027s actual landing spot \\u0022off the parent\\u0027s own run\\u0022 and only asked a live source once the run\\u0027s recorded base already disagreed with the project\\u0027s own base branch. That gate misses the one shape it exists for: GitHub retargets a mid-stack parent\\u0027s own pull request onto the project\\u0027s base exactly the way it retargets a stacked child\\u0027s, the moment the parent\\u0027s own parent branch is deleted (Decisions Log #186), and nothing on this platform\\u0027s records is rewritten when that happens \\u2014 so a parent silently retargeted and merged that way reads a recorded base already equal to the project\\u0027s own, indistinguishable on the record alone from an ordinary, never-stacked merge. Gating the live ask on a mismatch therefore let exactly that parent sail past \\u0060ParentMergedElsewhere\\u0060 and reach a mechanical retarget-and-replay onto a base missing the grandparent\\u0027s own work. The local arm now asks the live source whenever the parent has merged, unconditionally, record or no record; the remote arm, whose own recorded base is already a live GitHub read captured in the same \\u0060gh pr view\\u0060 that established the merge itself, makes no further provider call, which keeps \\u0060RemoteStackedParentSweep\\u0060 the single reader of a remote parent. \\u0060ResolveActualMergedIntoAsync\\u0060\\u0027s own record-based fallback tier also moved behind its git-reachability tier rather than ahead of it, since a freshly observed containment proof outranks a static open-time record whenever the live read itself cannot be made. Reserved for slice two: the catch-up rebase choreography a Delivered parent\\u0027s own post-delivery churn demands, which is #146 below. The *earlier dispatch point* this entry also reserved for it \\u2014 the child starting at the parent\\u0027s build-complete-before-review \\u2014 was **dropped outright** by Brian\\u0027s ruling of 2026-08-28 late evening: \\u0060Delivered\\u0060 is the dispatch point, full stop, and #146 implements only the churn half. **Does this block the later vision?** No \\u2014 the whole feature is additive on nullable/blank-defaulting fields (\\u0060TaskAdded.StackedOnTaskId\\u0060, \\u0060TaskRevised.StackedOnTaskId\\u0060, \\u0060TaskReopened.StackReplayUpstreamCommit\\u0060/\\u0060StackReplayOntoCommit\\u0060, \\u0060RunDispatched.BaseBranch\\u0060/\\u0060BaseCommit\\u0060) plus one informational run event (\\u0060StackedPullRequestRetargeted\\u0060), a task that never declares an edge is byte-for-byte unchanged in prompt and behaviour, and the one provider write went onto the existing inspector seam rather than a new one. The parked shape it does not foreclose is a stack as a first-class object \\u2014 an \\u0060h9k stack\\u0060 surface, ordering across three or more levels, reordering \\u2014 which the pairwise edges
